flags.detail: pipeline/archive.py and its workflow step are merged in this round. The archive's first entry is created by the first scheduled run; until then no multi-day history exists.

flags.title: Reserve moves are in official news, not in the injury report
flags.detail: The Dolphins' QB Malik Willis moved to injured reserve, and the Patriots placed RB TreVeyon Henderson on injured reserve, per official news links. The report does not show reserve status, so 'not listed' is not 'available'.

flags.title: The price store stamps every row with the build time, not a capture time
flags.detail: src/console/feed.py build_price_snapshots writes one build timestamp into captured_at_utc, open_captured_at_utc and close_captured_at_utc. The committed rows read 2026-11-14T20:48:22Z. A rebuild on 2026-11-15 rewrites all 18,902 rows to 2026-11-15T18:20:14Z, and the row order changes. The mirror publishes no capture time (its own note says so), so these fields must not be presented as capture times. Found during the R4-1 console rebuild, which was not committed.

flags.title: Replacement-depth coverage does not reconcile with the 31-club and 897-slot figures on the landing page
flags.detail: data/depth/replacement_depth.csv has 78 rows across 20 clubs. data/depth/replacement_depth_summary.json reports 897 slots from data/pipeline/depth_charts.json, which lists 31 clubs (all except Houston, see R4-F09). The club count in the replacement file is not explained by the depth charts. Not reconciled this round.

metrics.demotion_status: Defined and pre-registered. Trigger thresholds T2-T4 are proposed defaults awaiting owner ratification (decision Q-26). T1 and T5 are boolean rules and need no threshold. Nothing here is invented data: this is a policy definition, and every threshold is labelled as proposed where it is a choice rather than a fact.
